meta.title: Number of ratings versus reliability: recommended analysis for the sparse, randomly assigned rating design
meta.purpose: Reference for verifying that the manuscript's analysis of reliability as a function of the number of ratings per action is carried out and described as recommended. Replaces the earlier version of judges_vs_reliability_reference.json.
meta.provenance: Recommendation based on the design described by the author; nothing here was computed on the manuscript's data. Action counts are as reported by the author.

design.assignment: The number of ratings per action was assigned at random; there is no pattern in which actions were rated more or less often.
design.crossed_block: No action was rated by all judges. The largest fully crossed block has about 14 judges and about 10 actions.
design.crossed_block_verdict: Not usable for this analysis: an empirical reliability from about 10 scores would be mostly noise. Random assignment makes a crossed block unnecessary.

component_1_grouped_analysis.justification: Because the number of ratings was assigned at random, each group is a random sample of all actions. Reliability by number of ratings is therefore a valid design-based result, not only a description.
component_1_grouped_analysis.method: Group actions by the number of ratings received and compute the reliability of the EAP scores within each group.

report_both_versions_per_group.empirical_reliability: Var(EAP) / (Var(EAP) + mean(PSD^2)), computed within the group
report_both_versions_per_group.expected_relation: With random assignment the two should agree, because score variance plus mean error variance is close to 1. A divergence indicates that the group's actions are not typical of all actions.

group_sizes.adequate: Groups with 1 to 7 ratings (114 to 2627 actions each).
group_sizes.thin: Groups with 8, 9, 10 and more than 10 ratings (66, 36, 20, 20 actions). Pool them or show them with wide intervals.

component_1_grouped_analysis.uncertainty: Bootstrap confidence intervals over actions for every point.

component_2_thinning_within_actions.role: Validation. Recovers what a crossed block would have provided by subsampling ratings per action instead of judges per block.
component_2_thinning_within_actions.common_setup: Judge parameters are kept fixed at the estimates from the full model; only the scoring is repeated.

thinning.method: Take the actions with five or more ratings. Randomly keep n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 of each action's ratings, rescore by EAP, and compute the empirical reliability at each n. Repeat over many random draws.
thinning.advantage: The same actions appear at every n, which the grouped analysis cannot offer.

split_halves.method: Split each action's ratings into two disjoint random sets of n ratings, score both sets, and correlate the two scores across actions. Repeat over many random splits.
split_halves.interpretation: With random judge assignment, this correlation directly estimates the reliability of a score based on n ratings.
advantages: No part-whole overlap between the two scores.
Depends little on the model's own standard errors, so it is the check that relies least on the model being right.
split_halves.support: 1 vs 1, 2 vs 2 and 3 vs 3 are well supported; 4 vs 4 is usable; 5 vs 5 is too small to rely on.

component_3_model_based_curve.role: Ties the results together and extends them beyond the range where the data are dense.
component_3_model_based_curve.method: For each n, draw sets of n judges, sum their information functions I(theta), and compute the expected reliability as the average of I(theta) / (I(theta) + 1) over a N(0,1) distribution of theta. Plot against n.
component_3_model_based_curve.judge_sampling: Sample judges in proportion to the number of ratings each contributed, so that the curve mimics the real design.
component_3_model_based_curve.status_of_extension: Values beyond the range with dense data are model-based projections, not observed results.

classical_reference.method: Spearman-Brown curve, rel(n) = n * r_1 / (1 + (n - 1) * r_1), from a single-rating reliability r_1.
classical_reference.role: Classical reference line on the same figure.

content: Grouped reliabilities as points with confidence intervals.
Split-half correlations as a second set of points.
Spearman-Brown curve as the classical reference.

interpretation.agreement: If the three analyses agree for n = 1 to about 7, the relationship is well supported in that range, with a model-based projection beyond it.
interpretation.disagreement: A gap between the split-half points and the other two is informative, because the split-half values depend least on the model being correct.

checks_for_the_manuscript: States that the number of ratings per action was randomly assigned, as the basis for treating the grouped analysis as design-based.
Does not base the analysis on the fully crossed block of about 10 actions.
Reports both reliability versions per group, or states which one is shown.
Pools or clearly marks the thin groups (8 or more ratings) and gives confidence intervals.
States that judge parameters were held fixed when rescoring thinned or split ratings.
Split-half sets are disjoint; scores are not correlated with scores that include the same ratings.
Does not rely on the 5 vs 5 split (40 actions).
States how judges were sampled for the model-based curve.
Labels every curve or point set by type (model-based, grouped empirical, split-half, Spearman-Brown).
Presents values beyond the dense range as projections.
